test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 09 Jul, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Judicial Review, a salient feature of the Constitution of India, has been borrowed from which of the following countries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The US**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Judicial Review** in India has been borrowed from the **United States** Constitution.
 
• It is a process under which executive or legislative actions are subject to review by the judiciary.
 
• This feature helps in ensuring the constitutionality of laws and acts as a check on the powers of the legislature and executive.
 
• The concept of Judicial Review in India is enshrined in **Article 13** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It plays a crucial role in protecting the fundamental rights of citizens and maintaining the supremacy of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• c
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.
